faq.q: How does ghost.claims integrate with @theme.tools/blog and PlateJS?
faq.a: Every article on ghost.claims is authored as a canonical Post Document (schemaVersion 1) whose body interleaves Markdown prose with {{widget:<id>}} and {{figure:<id>}} tokens. Public pages render server-side via @theme.tools/blog/site, @theme.tools/blog/widgets, @theme.tools/blog/media, and @theme.tools/blog/markdown with zero editor JS overhead. Clicking Edit Post opens /blog/sensor-telemetry-web-dossier/edit, which mounts the React 19 + PlateJS editor island (/blog/editor.js) backed by @theme.tools/blog/editor (toPlateValue, fromPlateValue, and applyPlateValue).

faq.q: Why did ghost.claims replace standalone HTML blog templates with @theme.tools/blog?
faq.a: Standalone HTML templates create immediate design drift, lack structured widget validation, and cannot be edited in PlateJS. Sourcing SITE_CSS, WIDGET_CSS, MEDIA_CSS, CMS_CSS, navigation, evidence badges, table of contents, and PlateJS serialization directly from @theme.tools/blog guarantees a single cohesive magazine experience across all 52 estate domains.

faq.q: How does lossless round-tripping work between Markdown and PlateJS in @theme.tools/blog/editor?
faq.a: toPlateValue() splits the post's Markdown around {{widget:<id>}} and {{figure:<id>}} lines into MarkdownBlockNode, WidgetNode, and FigureNode elements. In the PlateJS editor, prose blocks are edited smoothly while structured widgets and figures remain protected void cards. On save, fromPlateValue() and applyPlateValue() reassemble the Markdown and structured arrays without losing a single attribute.

faq.q: How does ghost.claims keep edge latency below 50ms while running strict validation?
faq.a: By compiling Zod schemas, Hono RPC route trees, and @theme.tools/blog SSR functions inside lightweight V8 isolates on Cloudflare Workers, validation and HTML rendering execute in microseconds at the nearest edge Point of Presence.

faq.q: What happens if an upstream AI provider or telemetry collector experiences an outage?
faq.a: All external AI and observability calls in ghost.claims are wrapped in a strict 2,500ms timeout with a 3-strike circuit breaker and local fail-open JSONL spooling. User-facing routes on ghost.claims continue serving traffic without interruption.

faq.q: Where can I inspect or edit this article on ghost.claims?
faq.a: You can read the rendered article at https://ghost.claims/blog/sensor-telemetry-web-dossier, inspect the PlateJS block AST at https://ghost.claims/blog/api/sensor-telemetry-web-dossier, or open the interactive PlateJS block editor directly at https://ghost.claims/blog/sensor-telemetry-web-dossier/edit.

data.title: Key architectural takeaways
items: To engineer sensor telemetry web dossier reliably on ghost.claims, eliminate state drift by pairing Cloudflare Workers V8 isolates with inline Hono RPC routes and strict Zod input contracts.

Source every blog layout, widget, media figure, and CMS affordance directly from @theme.tools/blog (@theme.tools/blog/site, @theme.tools/blog/widgets, @theme.tools/blog/media, @theme.tools/blog/cms) rather than ad-hoc HTML templates.

Author articles as structured Post Documents (schemaVersion 1) with {{widget:<id>}} and {{figure:<id>}} placement tokens that round-trip losslessly through @theme.tools/blog/editor (toPlateValue / fromPlateValue) for in-browser PlateJS editing.
Enforce a strict 2,500ms fail-open circuit breaker on all outbound Langfuse and telemetry spans so observability outages never block user-facing requests on ghost.claims.
Verify every release across all 16 interactive visual states and 6 responsive Playwright breakpoints (320px to 1920px) before promoting to production and purging the Cloudflare CDN cache.

data.title: Lossless PlateJS & @theme.tools/blog integration invariant
data.body: Every article on ghost.claims is stored as a structured @theme.tools/blog Post Document containing Markdown prose interleaved with {{widget:<id>}} and {{figure:<id>}} placement tokens on their own lines. When an authorized editor opens /blog/sensor-telemetry-web-dossier/edit, @theme.tools/blog/editor converts the post via toPlateValue() into a sequence of MarkdownBlockNode, WidgetNode, and FigureNode blocks inside the React 19 + PlateJS editor. Saving runs fromPlateValue() and applyPlateValue() to validate every token and preserve widget and figure payloads without loss.

data.title: Standardizing ghost.claims on @theme.tools/blog and PlateJS: the honest trade
pros: Zero visual or structural drift across all 52 estate domains — every site inherits SITE_CSS, WIDGET_CSS, MEDIA_CSS, and CMS_CSS from @theme.tools/blog.
Public readers receive fast, zero-editor-runtime semantic HTML SSR while editors get a rich, lazy-loaded PlateJS block editor on demand.
Strict build-time validation via normalizeBlogContent() rejects dangling widget tokens, duplicate IDs, or empty widget shapes before deployment.
Built-in dark/light reading mode, CSS scroll-timeline reading progress, table of contents, and device-local reading list bookmarks.
cons: Requires every widget and figure placement token ({{widget:<id>}}, {{figure:<id>}}) to appear on its own line in Markdown.
Strict widget validation (WidgetError) rejects half-authored or empty widget arrays at build time rather than rendering placeholders.
Adding a brand-new cross-site widget type happens upstream in @theme.tools/blog rather than via ad-hoc inline HTML in consumer repos.
Editors must preserve non-empty prose or valid widget tokens when saving through the PlateJS serialization boundary.

data.quote: If a blog article in ghost.claims cannot round-trip losslessly through toPlateValue and fromPlateValue in @theme.tools/blog/editor, it is an ad-hoc template — not part of the editorial system.

data.title: Six-step @theme.tools/blog & PlateJS verification runbook for ghost.claims

steps.title: Author the canonical Post Document
steps.body: Define schemaVersion 1 metadata, evidence provenance, FAQ items, figures, widgets, and Markdown body with {{widget:<id>}} and {{figure:<id>}} tokens in content/posts/sensor-telemetry-web-dossier.json.

steps.title: Verify normalizeBlogContent & PlateJS round-trip
steps.body: Run normalizeBlogContent(post), toPlateValue(post), and fromPlateValue(plateValue) from @theme.tools/blog/editor to prove 100% lossless AST serialization.

steps.title: Render through @theme.tools/blog/site & widgets
steps.body: Compile the index and article HTML using SITE_CSS, WIDGET_CSS, MEDIA_CSS, CMS_CSS, renderSiteNav, renderArticle, renderWidget, renderMedia, and renderMarkdown.

steps.title: Wire CMS affordances & PlateJS editor routes
steps.body: Expose renderAddAffordance on /blog and renderEditAffordance on /blog/sensor-telemetry-web-dossier, backed by /blog/sensor-telemetry-web-dossier/edit, /blog/editor.js, and /blog/api/sensor-telemetry-web-dossier.

steps.title: Audit across 6 Playwright breakpoints
steps.body: Verify 320px, 375px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px, and 1920px viewports for zero console errors, zero axe-core violations, and WCAG AAA OKLCH contrast.

steps.title: Deploy to Cloudflare Edge & verify HTTP 200
steps.body: Publish to Cloudflare Workers, purge CDN cache, and verify HTTP 200 OK on https://ghost.claims/blog, https://ghost.claims/blog/sensor-telemetry-web-dossier, and https://ghost.claims/blog/sensor-telemetry-web-dossier/edit.

terms.def: The lossless sequence of PlateJS block nodes (MarkdownBlockNode, WidgetNode, FigureNode) produced by toPlateValue() and consumed by fromPlateValue().
A standalone line in a post's Markdown body that normalizeBlogContent() binds to a structured BlogWidget rendered by @theme.tools/blog/widgets or @theme.tools/blog/media.
The accessible + Add Blog Post and ✎ Edit Post controls rendered by renderAddAffordance() and renderEditAffordance() using CMS_CSS.
Chained route definitions on a Hono instance that preserve end-to-end TypeScript request and response type inference across client and edge boundaries.
An observability wrapper that enforces AbortSignal.timeout(2500) and spools spans locally after 3 consecutive upstream failures so user traffic never stalls.
Perceptually uniform color and design tokens defined in cylindrical OKLCH space to guarantee consistent contrast across dark and light reading modes.
